boards.title: Your First Weekend at Northwestern University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented to Northwestern’s Evanston campus and lakefront through named places and recurring public activities.

cards.title: Start at Weber Arch
cards.subtitle: A symbolic entrance to the Evanston campus
cards.notes: Begin your walk at the arch, then use it as a reference point while you connect the south-campus landmarks on either side of Sheridan Road.
cards.short_summary: An easy first landmark for establishing your campus bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern identifies Weber Arch as the symbolic entrance used during Wildcat Welcome for incoming students.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow normal campus and pedestrian rules.

cards.title: See the day’s message at The Rock
cards.subtitle: Near University Hall on Sheridan Road
cards.notes: Pause to look at the current paint layer and read the student expression on display; treat it as a landmark rather than a surface to alter yourself.
cards.short_summary: A visible, changing record of campus expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern documents The Rock as a student-moderated canvas for slogans, student-group advertising, activism, and other messages.
cards.access_notes: Located off Sheridan Road directly south of University Hall; painting is governed by university policy.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Norris
cards.subtitle: 1999 Campus Drive
cards.notes: Use the student center as your indoor reset: check posted programming, find campus services, and choose a next stop before heading back outside.
cards.short_summary: The campus community hub for programs, services, and gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern describes Norris University Center as providing spaces for community engagement and cultural inclusion.
cards.access_notes: Check the Norris site for current building hours and event details.

cards.title: Look in on Wild Roots Garden
cards.subtitle: At Norris University Center
cards.notes: Walk by the student-directed growing space and use its updates to learn about gardening, sustainable food, or any opportunities to participate.
cards.short_summary: A student-directed garden connecting food and sustainability.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern says Wild Roots is a student-directed garden growing fresh produce for Northwestern and Evanston communities using sustainable practices.
cards.access_notes: Garden participation and programming may be seasonal; follow current Norris updates.

cards.title: Take the lakefront path
cards.subtitle: Northwestern’s Lake Michigan peninsula
cards.notes: Make this the unhurried part of the route: walk the lakefront, orient yourself to the shoreline, and leave time to sit or take photos in daylight.
cards.short_summary: A lakeside campus walk with shoreline and skyline views.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern describes the Lakefill as the part of campus on a peninsula directly next to Lake Michigan.
cards.access_notes: Use designated pedestrian paths and observe posted lakefront conditions.

cards.title: Step into the Block Museum
cards.subtitle: Northwestern’s campus art museum
cards.notes: Check the current exhibitions before you go, then spend time with one gallery rather than trying to cover everything on a first visit.
cards.short_summary: A focused indoor art stop on the Evanston campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Block Museum of Art is Northwestern University’s art museum and offers free admission.
cards.source_title: Visit the Block Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Review the museum’s current visitor hours and exhibition schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Walk through Deering Library
cards.subtitle: 1937 Sheridan Road
cards.notes: Enter from Sheridan Road or through University Library, then take in the historic interior and note the special collections housed in the building.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus library building with distinctive collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern states that Deering Library opened in 1933 and now houses several distinctive collections.
cards.access_notes: Enter through the west-facing Sheridan Road doors or Level 1 of University Library; check current hours.

cards.title: Slow down in Shakespeare Garden
cards.subtitle: East of Sheridan Road near Garrett Place
cards.notes: Take the garden paths at a quiet pace and look for the sundial, stonework, and plantings associated with Shakespeare’s works.
cards.short_summary: A historic, landscaped pause between north- and south-campus stops.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern’s campus map says Shakespeare Garden contains more than 50 plants mentioned in William Shakespeare’s works and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.access_notes: The garden is free and open to the public; use established paths and respect plantings.

cards.title: Plan a Friday stargazing stop
cards.subtitle: Dearborn Observatory, Evanston campus
cards.notes: If your weekend includes Friday, check tour availability early; arrive ready for stairs and weather, then join the listed walk-in observing session.
cards.short_summary: A free public observing stop for a Friday-night campus visit.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern offers free public Friday-night tours at Dearborn Observatory, with a walk-in session at 10–11 PM from April through September.
cards.access_notes: Current April–September walk-in tours are Fridays, 10–11 PM; the observatory is not ADA accessible because the dome requires multiple staircases.

cards.title: Close with a campus game session
cards.subtitle: Norris University Center Game Room
cards.notes: For a low-key indoor finish, bring your NetID and check station availability; weekly esports practices can limit general-use computers on some evenings.
cards.short_summary: A student-only, computer-gaming option inside Norris.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern says Nexus Gaming Lounge is free for Northwestern students, requires a university NetID, and has a ten-hour weekly usage limit.
cards.access_notes: Northwestern students need a NetID; Wednesday and Thursday esports activity can reduce general station availability.
